intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Tonight's roll was seed 1517729463. Here is each roll and what came of it, live from Clover's kitchen. Season to taste.

rolls.became: Clover, a white rabbit in an apron who narrates every moment of its life like a cooking show, to an audience that isn't there yet. One ear up, one flopped, for drama. It wants to be seen by everyone, and it has a plan.

Great-Aunt Kiki's recipe card is held to the fridge by a magnet, folded so the only words that show are FERMENT … UMBRELLAS … LET RISE. Clover takes it literally. So does the game: an umbrella's canopy is a skin that traps bubbles, so a fermented umbrella proves like dough and puffs up into a dome that floats.

Eleven kinds, each bigger than the last: a plain black brolly (it lifts the kitchen 8 cm), golf, doorman's, beach, café, patio, market parasol, a bandstand roof, a wedding marquee, a stadium roof and a circus big top. You can watch them change in the crocks and in the bouquet over the roof.
When an umbrella has puffed into a full dome, swipe across its crock and it flies up and ties itself onto the bouquet. One swipe can flick a whole shelf. Tapping and the space bar work too.

Fame here is a matter of geometry: the higher the kitchen, the farther away it can be seen, so more people look up. The meter counts the onlookers, from 12 neighbours to everyone on Earth, who can all see the Moon.

Flick an umbrella before it has puffed and gravity wins: it flops back into the crock. But gravity weakens the farther you get from the middle of the Earth, so every umbrella lifts the kitchen further than the last. The readout shows it falling from 1.00 g. Near the end, the Moon's own gravity takes over and pulls you in.

rolls.value: one long build that eats everything you make
rolls.became: The Rise. Every umbrella you make goes up into the bouquet, and the bouquet carries the kitchen past the rooftops, a kite, the rain cloud, a jet, the edge of space, a space station and the satellites, all the way to the Moon. Nothing you make is ever spent: it all goes up.

The Recipe: twenty-seven steps in order, and only the next one can be bought (you can see the one after it, too). Bigger umbrellas, livelier cultures (Doris the sourdough starter, kefir grains, a kombucha mother, koji, a ginger bug, Kiki's old brine), things for the sous-chefs, and a few odd purchases that do nothing at all. Tips pay for them: onlookers drop coins in a basket on a very long string, the way you'd tip a busker.

rolls.value: a choice you can't take back changes the world
rolls.became: Two kilometres up the kitchen wedges into a rain cloud. Stir the starter into it and it rains on the town: every umbrella in town ferments and floats up to join you, the town stays soaked, and their umbrellas drift past the window all the way to the Moon. Or bottle the cloud and hang it under the kitchen as a brine tank: umbrellas puff twice as fast, and the town gets clear skies for the rest of the trip.
8.1 billion onlookers at the top, tips in the billions per second, and 384,400 km of altitude. The meter climbs by powers of ten.

About an hour and a half, over a couple of sittings. Paper-doll sous-chefs keep sweeping their shelves while you're away, at a tenth of the speed, and they stop short of each new sight: Clover wouldn't want to miss one.
Great-Aunt Kiki, whose card started all this, and who kept a box of something by the door.

rolls.value: a household ritual of the season
rolls.became: Kimjang, the late-autumn weekend when Korean families make kimchi together for the winter. The neighbours are back from theirs and lend Clover their big clay onggi jars. The clay breathes, so umbrellas puff faster, and the crocks on the shelves turn into onggi.

On the Moon, live to the whole planet, Clover finally unfolds Kiki's card all the way. It's a recipe for plum fizz: ferment the plums a week, then garnish with the little paper umbrellas. The bowl of plums, the empty little glass and the cocktail umbrella that lifted nothing have been sitting in the kitchen all game.

rolls.value: the small thing was the point
rolls.became: The last flick of the game is the smallest: the tiny paper umbrella, into one small glass. Eight billion people watch a rabbit make a drink, and the next day nobody talks about the flying kitchen. They all want to know about the little umbrella.

Everything is cut from flat paper and casts a hard little shadow: the kitchen is a cutaway dollhouse, the sky is strips of paper that darken as you climb, and the sous-chefs are paper dolls with tall hats.
Four colours by Poltergasm: ink, slate, rose-grey and paper white. That's the whole sky, from a pale morning over town to the black of space.

A lazy bossa nova in E phrygian, with nylon guitar, upright bass, flute, a rim click and a shaker. The F over E gives it a little Spanish drama, which suits Clover. It gets dreamier in space, and every sound effect is in the same key: the flick, the bubbles, the coins in the basket.
“See how it domes? That's the bubbles. That's the drama.” Clover talks to the onlookers the whole way up, with darlings, here's-one-I-flicked-earlier and a theme song it wrote about itself.

outro: Garnish with a little paper umbrella. Serves everyone who looks up.
